## REQ-RES-CONFIG-001

**An asset may have several Config DataSets**

A component may publish several Config DataSets per asset, one per context, each with its own Filter (REQ-RES-CONFIG-015).

- Keyword: MAY
- Levels: L1 MAY · L2 MAY · L3 MAY
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device

- Refs: MG 8.3.3, MG 9.1.3
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3-64a9097d, MG-9.1.3-c463268f

> Several configuration DataSetMessages may exist for an asset.
> — MG 9.1.3

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-002

**Structure of the Config DataSet (Pub)**

The Payload of a published Config DataSetMessage contains one or more groups – keys &lt;GroupName> whose value is a Group object – and optionally the key Context. A Group contains Name (LocalizedText), optionally Description (LocalizedText) and one or more configuration objects – keys &lt;ConfigName> whose value is a Config object. A Config object contains Type, Value and Name (LocalizedText) and optionally Unit (String), DefaultValue, Mandatory (Boolean, default false), Sensitive (Boolean, default false), Description (LocalizedText) and Validation. A Validation object contains the optional keys Length (UInt32), Min and Max (Real, a JSON number), Pattern (String) and Values (array of String). Context contains Name (LocalizedText) and optionally Description (LocalizedText). Config, Validation and Context objects contain no other keys.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 8.3.3, MG 8.3.3.1, MG 9.1.3, SF-084
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3-1c34a2be, MG-8.3.3-565fc688, MG-8.3.3-c25cf82c, MG-8.3.3.1-0a897b4b, MG-8.3.3.1-126ff9aa, MG-8.3.3.1-23cbfa5a, MG-8.3.3.1-27f5627b, MG-8.3.3.1-29da9752, MG-8.3.3.1-2b8af458, MG-8.3.3.1-2bcfa794, MG-8.3.3.1-3252fe76, MG-8.3.3.1-39df3233, MG-8.3.3.1-4c862c5c, MG-8.3.3.1-51d6f600, MG-8.3.3.1-6015d8a2, MG-8.3.3.1-a6e70e34, MG-8.3.3.1-ab90ce46, MG-8.3.3.1-af59cd36, MG-8.3.3.1-b91fda59, MG-8.3.3.1-bb506b94, MG-8.3.3.1-be3ae5c6, MG-8.3.3.1-ccfb0db5, MG-8.3.3.1-ce7454d2, MG-8.3.3.1-d03cc921, MG-8.3.3.1-d7495ce2, MG-8.3.3.1-d8646dba, MG-8.3.3.1-db47c71a, MG-8.3.3.1-ead395b9, MG-8.3.3.1-f52ec9eb, MG-8.3.3.1-fc37558b, MG-8.3.3.1-ff239c31

> The complete Config object has the same structure for the methods Pub and Set. However, they differ in which properties are mandatory.
> — MG 8.3.3

> The keys of the Payload other than Context are Group objects, the keys of a Group other than Name and Description are Config objects. Config, Validation and Context objects contain no other keys than listed.
> — MG 8.3.3

> A configuration object can only be added to a Group. Therefore at least one Group is mandatory, even when it contains only one single configuration object or several objects, which are not tightly coupled.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> Several Group objects can be added to a single DataSetMessage of type Config.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> A DisplayName for this Group object shall be given as localized text.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> A DisplayName for this Config object shall be given as localized text.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: The nesting (payload → &lt;GroupName>/Context, Group → Name/Description/&lt;ConfigName>, Config → Type … Validation, Validation → Length … Values) is the structure overview of MG 8.3.3 (SF-084 (a)); Values is an "Array of String" (SF-084 (c)). Min and Max ("Real") are JSON numbers. Field presence and types per REQ-CMP-025/026; LocalizedText per REQ-MSG-040. Sensitive values are masked (REQ-RES-CONFIG-024).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-003

**Structure of the Config DataSet in a Set**

The Payload of the Config DataSetMessage of a Set has the structure of REQ-RES-CONFIG-002 with these differences: the Name of a Group and Type and Name of a Config object are optional; Value stays mandatory in every Config object. It contains at least one group with at least one configuration object and may contain a subset of the groups of the addressed Config DataSet and, within a group, of its configuration objects (mandatory objects: REQ-RES-CONFIG-011); further properties are optional and may be taken from the published Config.

- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3, MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3, SF-084, SF-086
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-004

**Character set of GroupName and ConfigName**

Every GroupName and ConfigName is a non-empty string of the characters a–z, A–Z, 0–9, "-" and "_" that does not start with a digit or "-". A GroupName is not "Context", a ConfigName neither "Name" nor "Description".

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, SF-084
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-1e400088, MG-8.3.3.1-c6309630, MG-8.3.3.1-cbc11847, MG-8.3.3.1-e2f7095a, MG-8.3.3.1-ec257974, MG-8.3.3.1-f1d934b9, MG-8.3.3.2-04062350, MG-8.3.3.2-47e3c53f, MG-8.3.3.2-7c86dbf5, MG-8.3.3.2-9e8bf02f, MG-8.3.3.2-b0867894, MG-8.3.3.2-e7996b9d

> To avoid problems on JSON parsing in different languages, the GroupName must contain only the characters &lt;a..z>, &lt;A..Z>, &lt;0..9>, &lt;-> and &lt;_>. The GroupName must not start with a number (0..9) or with a minus (-).
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> To avoid problems on JSON parsing in different languages, the ConfigName must contain only the characters &lt;a..z>, &lt;A..Z>, &lt;0..9>, &lt;-> and &lt;_>. The ConfigName must not start with a number (0..9) or with a minus (-).
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> A GroupName must not be Context.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> A ConfigName must not be Name or Description.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: The reserved names (Context; Name, Description) avoid keys that cannot be told apart from the properties of the same level (SF-084 (b)). The checker reports names outside the character set.

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-005

**Groups and configuration objects are defined by the owner only**

Only the component that owns a Config DataSet defines its groups and configuration objects; a Set uses the published GroupNames and ConfigNames and does not add, rename or remove groups or configuration objects.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-59c566b4, MG-8.3.3.1-70cb55b3, MG-8.3.3.2-5920d940, MG-8.3.3.2-c2918061, MG-9.1.3-ddbafedb

> The group name must not be changed from outside the service specifying it, but the object group has elements which allow read/write access!
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> The config name must not be changed from outside the service specifying it, but the object Config has elements which allow read/write access!
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> As the device or application providing the resource is the owner of the configuration object, it is the only instance which can remove objects from within the config object.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: A Set with an unknown group or configuration object is rejected (REQ-RES-CONFIG-023, REQ-CMP-043). Names are compared exactly (case-sensitive); the device example of MG B1.1.3 uses "unit" and "common" in every message since SF-088 (a).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-006

**Type is one of five OPC UA base types**

The Type of a configuration object is one of Boolean, ByteString, DateTime, Number and String (subset of the OPC UA base types, Part 5 12.2.1 Table 154 and Part 3 8).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device, requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-0c91156e, MG-8.3.3.2-6e8b3808

> A subset of OPC UA base types, defined in OPC UA Part 5-12.2.1-Table 154 and more detailed in Part 3-8 shall be used as Type.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> The allowed subset is Boolean, ByteString, DateTime, Number and String.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: A requester that repeats Type in a Set uses the published one (REQ-RES-CONFIG-023). Further restrictions of a type (e.g. a value range) are expressed with Validation; MG 8.3.3.1 mentions arbitrary data types via Pattern.

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-007

**Value and DefaultValue are strings in the representation of Type**

Value and DefaultValue are JSON strings. A non-empty one represents a value of Type: Boolean "true" or "false", Number a decimal number in JSON number syntax, DateTime an ISO 8601 date-time (RFC 3339), ByteString base64 and String any text. An empty Value means that the configuration object is not set. Exception: the mask of a sensitive configuration object (REQ-RES-CONFIG-024/025) is not interpreted with Type.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device, requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, SF-084
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-7641aa0a, MG-8.3.3.1-fda68158, MG-8.3.3.2-5ece4201, MG-8.3.3.2-c0ca9c8c

> The Value of a configuration item must always be a string, which must be interpreted with help of the Type information.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> The DefaultValue of a configuration item must always be a string, which must be interpreted with help of the Type information.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> Each type is presented as string in the Value and the DefaultValue:
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> An empty string means that the value is not set.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> Exception: the mask `********` of a sensitive Config object (see Sensitive).
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: The representations per Type are listed in MG 8.3.3.1/8.3.3.2 (SF-084 (d), in line with the JSON encoding of OPC UA Part 6 5.4). The checker checks them where Type and Value are in the same object (Pub, Set with Type) and skips the mask of a sensitive object.

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-008

**A set Value satisfies the Validation**

A non-empty Value satisfies the Validation of its configuration object: at most Length characters, for Type Number a number between Min and Max (inclusive), a match of the regular expression Pattern and one of Values, as far as these keys are given. The mask of a sensitive configuration object (REQ-RES-CONFIG-024/025) is not checked against the Validation.

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device, requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, SF-035, SF-084
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-17f15d4d, MG-8.3.3.1-4bc68317, MG-8.3.3.1-f17be68d, MG-8.3.3.2-6fb4d812, MG-8.3.3.2-8a6ca709, MG-8.3.3.2-d15fa833

> The Min contains the minimal value, a Value can get.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> The Max contains the maximum value, a Value can get.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> A type of enumeration to show, which values are allowed.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> The Length contains the max length of a Value, counted in characters.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: Length counts characters (Unicode code points); Min and Max apply to the Type Number (SF-084 (d)). Patterns should be interoperable (MG 8.3.3.1 note); the checker evaluates a Pattern with Go RE2 and skips patterns it cannot compile. A Set that violates the Validation is rejected (REQ-RES-CONFIG-023).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-009

**Unit is an EngineeringUnit DisplayName**

The Unit of a configuration object is the DisplayName of an EngineeringUnit of OPC UA Part 8 5.6.3 (UNECE Recommendation N° 20); a unit that does not exist there may be self-defined (preferably industry-specific).

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The configuration object has a unit.
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-8488db27, MG-8.3.3.1-f0f59ab3, MG-8.3.3.2-ee0cf174, MG-8.3.3.2-f0d82434

> The Unit should contain the DisplayName of one of the EngineeringUnits defined in OPC UA Part 8-5.6.3 (see UNECE Recommendation N° 20 for a good overview).
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> However, when a very rare unit does not exist in the list of EngineeringUnits, a self defined (or better industry specific) unit may be used here.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: The B1.1.3 device example had "Unit": "Temperature" (a quantity, no unit); removed with SF-088 (c).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-010

**A value is unset with an empty string, there is no Del**

A requester unsets ("deletes") a configuration value with a Set that carries an empty string as its Value; Config has no Del.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-225f710d, MG-8.3.3.2-4419a9e8, MG-9.1.3-3350ff5c, MG-9.1.3-516d732b

> To delete, or better, unset a configuration, the related value must be overwritten with an empty string.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> However, to “delete” or better unset a configured object, the sender must send a value with an empty string with the Set method.
> — MG 9.1.3

> To do so, the sender must send a Set with an empty value of the config object.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: Del Config is not allowed (matrix, REQ-TOP-013). Examples MG B1.1.3 "empty existing values".

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-011

**Mandatory configuration objects are contained in every Set of their group**

A configuration object with Mandatory = true is contained, with its Value, in every Set that contains its group; without Mandatory a configuration object is not mandatory (default false).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3, SF-086
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-269a6962, MG-8.3.3.1-629dca2b, MG-8.3.3.1-bc1d417b, MG-8.3.3.2-aeff2f0d, MG-8.3.3.2-ddc33ac3, MG-8.3.3.2-f3e06630, MG-9.1.3-1d957d86, MG-9.1.3-7c151900, MG-9.1.3-cf25bdf3

> If Mandatory is set to true, this Config object must be part of the Group in every Set which contains the Group, including its Value. An empty Value of a mandatory Config object is a valid message; the application may reject it with a status Event with the EventLevel Bad.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> If it does not exist, the default behavior is the same as Mandatory = false.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> A Set message is a partial update: it contains at least one group with at least one config element, and all config elements of a contained group which are mandatory ("Mandatory": true) must be provided!
> — MG 9.1.3

> The payload must contain the values of the mandatory config names of each contained group.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: An empty Value of a mandatory object is a valid Set; the application may reject it (REQ-RES-CONFIG-023) – B1.1.3 unsets the mandatory objects aut0-r3fr3sh and protocol (SF-086 (b)). A mandatory sensitive object can be sent with the mask (REQ-RES-CONFIG-025). Checkable only against the published Config (Mandatory flags), not per message.

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-012

**Front-ends hide the value of a sensitive configuration object**

An application that displays or edits configuration values (e.g. a web front-end) hides the value of a configuration object with Sensitive = true (type "password"), also when a new value is entered.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application displays or edits Config values.
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2, GL-ADR-021, SF-087
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-6ab60217, MG-8.3.3.1-e2e7bd23, MG-8.3.3.2-16781fc2

> In context with the available OPC UA base types, the OI4 Alliance is missing type "password" which can be used to hide the value of an object (e.g. in user interfaces, such as web front-ends) if necessary.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> Front-end applications should hide it as well, e.g. when a new value is entered.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: The Message Bus side is REQ-RES-CONFIG-024 (masking in every Pub) and REQ-RES-CONFIG-025 (mask in a Set). MAY → SHOULD with GL-ADR-021: the note of MG 8.3.3.1 recommends hiding the value in front-ends.

A component puts configuration objects that should be configured at once into one Group (e.g. group eth0 with ip_address, subnet_mask and standard_gateway).

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-0300b49d, MG-8.3.3.2-08b07130

> The Group helps to group configuration elements which should be configured at once, e.g. the group eth0 might contain configuration objects called ip_address, subnet_mask and standard_gateway.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: MG B1.1.3 "More complex example with two groups" (device1, common).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-014

**The group of common configuration objects is named common**

A component that collects common configuration objects in a Group names this group common.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 8.3.3.2
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-31537929, MG-8.3.3.1-d95dbf3d, MG-8.3.3.2-3be484bd, MG-8.3.3.2-6a638141

> It is best practice to name the Group that collects all common configuration objects common.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> Configuration objects in this group do not necessarily have to be grouped this way, but it is a way to make it clear that these objects belong to the "common settings".
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: Best practice → SHOULD (MG 1.2). B1.1.3 uses "common" in every message since SF-088 (a).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-015

**The Filter of a Config DataSet is its context name**

Each Config DataSet of an asset has its own Filter, the name of its context, used as topic Filter (REQ-TOP-022) and WriterGroupName (REQ-MSG-024). The Filter is chosen by the owning component, unique among the Config DataSets of the Source and independent of the requested Locale; Context.Name, if present, is its display name.

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 9.1.3, SF-035, SF-085
- Verification: d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-ed5a8ff3, MG-8.3.3.2-066620fe

> The Context helps to define an overall name for the included Group objects.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> The Filter (and the WriterGroupName) of a Config DataSetMessage is a stable, non-localized name chosen by the owner of the configuration, unique among the Config DataSetMessages of the Source. The Name of the Context is the display name of this Filter and can be localized; the Filter does not change with the requested Locale.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: Defined in MG 8.3.3.1/8.3.3.2 since SF-085; MG 9.1.3 writes the Filter as &lt;Filter>. In B1.1.3 Filter and Context.Name (en-US) are equal ("Network settings", "Overall device settings"). The definition has no keyword (implicit MUST).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-016

**Get Config carries no Config object**

A Get Config NetworkMessage contains no Config DataSetMessage; its Messages are empty or contain only the helper DataSets PaginationRequest and Locale.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Scope: MG 8.3.11, MG 8.3.12
- Refs: MG 9.1.3
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-10d496aa

> In combination with the method Get, the payload requires an empty NetworkMessage. The NetworkMessage can alternatively contain DataSetMessages for PaginationRequest (8.3.11.1 PaginationRequest) and Locale (8.3.12 Locale). A Config object is not included.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: Config has no Query (GL-ADR-020, REQ-QRY-001); new query parameters would need a PO order. Get with Locale: MG B1.1.3 (REQ-LOC-*).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-017

**Get Config is answered with all addressed Config DataSets**

A Get Config is answered with every Config DataSet addressed by the topic – without Source all Config DataSets of all assets of the component, with Source all of that asset, with Source and Filter that one – each in its own DataSetMessage of a single NetworkMessage published to the corresponding Pub topic.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: responder
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 9.1.3
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-b89cf9e2

> A topic such as Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Get/Config must trigger a publication of all available Config information, each in its own DataSetMessage added to a single NetworkMessage and published to the topic Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Pub/Config.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: Pagination of large answers is REQ-PAG-005, ReplyTo is REQ-MSG-015, the DataSetClassId REQ-MSG-010/011. A component without configuration answers with an empty list (REQ-CMP-041).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-018

**Pub Config carries Config DataSets and optionally Pagination**

A Pub Config NetworkMessage contains Config DataSetMessages and optionally the helper DataSet Pagination; it contains no PaginationRequest and no DataSetMessage of another resource.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 9.1.3
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-6859d952

> In combination with the method Pub, the payload contains DataSetMessages of type Config and optional Pagination (8.3.11.2 Pagination).
> — MG 9.1.3

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-019

**Set Config addresses exactly one Config DataSet**

A Set Config is sent to Set/Config/&lt;Source>/&lt;Filter> and its NetworkMessage contains exactly one Config DataSetMessage – the one addressed by the topic; several Config DataSets cannot be set at once.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Refs: MG 9.1.3, SF-079
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-8b7226fb, MG-9.1.3-b1dfe637, MG-9.1.3-c61b6741

> In combination with the method Set, the payload contains a single DataSetMessages of type Config. A topic with method Set must contain Resource, Source and Filter to be valid.
> — MG 9.1.3

> Each publication, using the method Set must be done explicitly.
> — MG 9.1.3

> Setting multiple DataSetMessages at once via Oi4v2/&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>/Set/Config is not possible due to security reasons because it can not be validated via an access control list by the Message Bus.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: PublisherId = requester (REQ-MSG-006); header of the DataSetMessage (DataSetWriterId of the addressed Config DataSet, Source, Filter, no SequenceNumber) per REQ-BUS-010. Which Config DataSets are writable is announced by the component (MG B1.1.3 note).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-020

**Set Config is protected by ACL**

The operator of the Message Bus prevents Set Config by unauthorized communication participants via the ACL of the broker.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: broker, platform
- Refs: MG 9.1.3
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-2444e5a1, MG-9.1.3-da560694

> To prevent write access by unauthorized communication participants, the operator must prevent this via ACL.
> — MG 9.1.3

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-021

**Status event after Set Config**

After a Set Config, the component publishes an Event of the category Status about the command on Pub/Event/&lt;Source>/Status/&lt;EventLevel> with the Source of the Set topic – mandatory from Level 2 on, recommended at Level 1.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Set for Config.
- Refs: MG 9.1.3, MG 7.4
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-c083f27e

> After a Set message arrived, the application must publish an Event message with status information about the Set command to the topic Pub/Event/&lt;Source>/Status/&lt;EventLevel> (8.3.6.1 Status) from compliance Level 2 on and should do so at Level 1 (7.4 Method Element) to provide feedback to the caller.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: Same obligation as REQ-TOP-014; ReplyTo and content per REQ-RES-EVENT-005. Example MG B1.1.3 (golden vector V-PAY-076).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-022

**Changed Config is published after a successful Set**

After a successful Set Config, the component publishes the new Config DataSet to Pub/Config/&lt;Source>/&lt;Filter> with the ReplyTo of the Set; the values of sensitive configuration objects are masked as in every Pub (REQ-RES-CONFIG-024).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Set for Config and the Set was successful.
- Refs: MG 9.1.3, GL-ADR-021
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-9.1.3-f44495ea

> If setting Config was successful, the new Config must be published to the Pub/Config[/&lt;Source>[/&lt;Filter>]] topic, according to the settings in PublicationList (8.3.8 PublicationList).
> — MG 9.1.3

> As in every publication of Config, the values of sensitive config elements are masked.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: Read like REQ-RES-DATA-012 and REQ-RES-PUBLIST-025: the answer to the Set goes to the topic with Source and Filter of the Set and contains the complete Config DataSet (REQ-RES-CONFIG-002); publications configured in the PublicationList follow on their own. General rule: REQ-BUS-006. Example: MG B1.1.3 "Pub explicit Config tag after a successful set request" (V-PAY-114).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-023

**A Set Config is applied completely or rejected**

A component applies a Set Config completely or not at all. It rejects the Set with a Status event of EventLevel Bad (REQ-RES-CONFIG-021) if the Set addresses a group or configuration object the Config DataSet does not have, changes a read-only property (every property except Value), lacks a mandatory configuration object of a contained group or carries a Value that does not represent its Type or violates its Validation (except the mask of a sensitive configuration object, REQ-RES-CONFIG-025); repeated unchanged read-only properties are accepted.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Set for Config.
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3, SF-035, SF-086
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.2-3a8c3bb0, MG-9.1.3-7d1e4d10

> The receiving application applies a Set completely or not at all
> — MG 8.3.3.2

> The Set is applied completely or not at all.
> — MG 9.1.3

> the Set must be rejected and the status Event must have the EventLevel Bad. Read-only properties which are repeated unchanged from Pub/Config are accepted.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: Stated in MG 8.3.3.2 and MG 9.1.3 since SF-086 (c)/(d), in line with PublicationList (REQ-RES-PUBLIST-016, SF-067 (f)) and REQ-CMP-043 (unknown object → Bad, e.g. BadNotFound, BadNotWritable, BadOutOfRange). The application may additionally reject a value it cannot apply (e.g. an empty Value of a mandatory object, REQ-RES-CONFIG-011).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-024

**Sensitive configuration values are masked in every Pub**

In every publication of a Config DataSet (answer to a Get, publication after a successful Set, publication configured in the PublicationList and any other publication), the publisher replaces a non-empty Value and a non-empty DefaultValue of a configuration object with Sensitive = true by the mask "********" (eight asterisks). An empty Value or DefaultValue is published as empty string. The mask is not interpreted with Type and not checked against Validation.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Config (REQ-CMP-035).
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.1, MG 9.1.3, GL-ADR-021, SF-087
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.1-3f9abadb, MG-8.3.3.1-72d258a9, MG-8.3.3.1-8912ceb4, MG-9.1.3-a94653f3

> If Sensitive is set to true, the publisher must replace a non-empty Value and a non-empty DefaultValue of this Config object by the mask `********` (eight asterisks) in every publication of the Config (Pub/Config) – in the answer to a Get, in the publication after a successful Set and in any other publication. An empty Value or DefaultValue is published as empty string, so a consumer can see whether the value is set.
> — MG 8.3.3.1

> In every publication of Config, the publisher must replace a non-empty Value and DefaultValue of a sensitive config element ("Sensitive": true) by the mask `********`
> — MG 9.1.3

> The value of a sensitive Config object is not published on the Message Bus; it can only be set
> — MG 8.3.3.1

Notes: New with GL-ADR-021 (SF-087). Levels follow the Config DataSet: a component that offers Config masks always. The checker reports a non-empty Value/DefaultValue other than the mask of a sensitive object in a Pub. Examples: MG B1.1.3 (V-PAY-099, V-PAY-114).

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-025

**The mask in a Set leaves a sensitive value unchanged**

A component that receives a Set Config whose Value of a configuration object with Sensitive = true is the mask "********" leaves this value unchanged and does not check the mask against Type and Validation. A sensitive value cannot be set to the mask itself; an empty Value unsets it as for every configuration object.

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: application, device
- Condition: The component offers Set for Config.
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3, GL-ADR-021, SF-035, SF-087
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.2-6f1a91a8, MG-8.3.3.2-c58a8f66

> If Sensitive is set to true, a Set whose Value of this Config object is the mask `********` leaves the value unchanged; the mask is not checked against Type and Validation. So a requester can send back a published Config unchanged and can include a mandatory sensitive Config object without knowing its value.
> — MG 8.3.3.2

> A Set with the mask `********` as Value of a sensitive config element leaves the value unchanged
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: New with GL-ADR-021 (SF-087). Levels as REQ-RES-CONFIG-023 (Set handling). A requester can send a published Config back unchanged (REQ-RES-CONFIG-003) and can include a mandatory sensitive object (REQ-RES-CONFIG-011) without knowing its value.

## REQ-RES-CONFIG-026

**The operator restricts read access to Set/Config**

Because a Set Config carries new sensitive values in clear text, the operator restricts, besides the write access, also the read access to the Set/Config topics via ACL.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Domain: platform · Applies to: broker, platform
- Condition: Components on the Message Bus offer Set for Config with sensitive configuration objects.
- Refs: MG 8.3.3.2, MG 9.1.3, GL-ADR-021, SF-087
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.3.3.2-62425f11, MG-9.1.3-ac3a3f16

> A Set carries a new sensitive value in clear text. Besides the write access, the operator should therefore also restrict the read access to the Set/Config topics via ACL
> — MG 8.3.3.2

> A Set carries new values of sensitive config elements in clear text. The operator should therefore also restrict the read access to the Set/Config topics via ACL.
> — MG 9.1.3

Notes: New with GL-ADR-021 (SF-087). Operator duty like the write ACL of REQ-RES-CONFIG-020; checked by the infrastructure CLI (D8).
